questiontext.text: In dynamic storage management, what does the free list track?

answer.text: The blocks of memory that are currently available for allocation

feedback.text: Correct — the free list records which blocks are free to hand out.

answer.text: The set of all currently reachable objects

feedback.text: Reachability is tracked during collection, not by the free list of available blocks.

answer.text: The order in which functions were called

feedback.text: That is the call stack, not the free list.
The free list is about heap blocks, not registers.

generalfeedback.text: The free list tracks the available (free) blocks of memory so the allocator can satisfy requests.

questiontext.text: Which pair are classic allocation strategies for choosing a free block?

feedback.text: Correct — first-fit takes the first big-enough block; best-fit takes the smallest big-enough block.
Those are graph traversals, not allocation strategies.
Those are not the standard allocation strategies discussed here.
Mark and sweep are garbage-collection phases, not block-selection strategies.

generalfeedback.text: Common allocation strategies include first-fit (first block that fits) and best-fit (smallest block that fits).

answer.text: Objects that are no longer reachable from the program

feedback.text: Correct — unreachable objects can never be used again, so their memory is reclaimed.

answer.text: Objects that are still reachable and in use

feedback.text: Reachable objects must be kept; only unreachable ones are reclaimed.

answer.text: The largest objects, regardless of reachability

feedback.text: Size is not the criterion; reachability is.
GC reclaims unreachable heap objects, not register contents.

generalfeedback.text: Garbage collection automatically reclaims unreachable objects using techniques like mark-and-sweep or reference counting.

questiontext.text: In mark-and-sweep collection, what happens during the two phases?

answer.text: The mark phase marks all reachable objects; the sweep phase reclaims the rest

feedback.text: Correct — mark identifies live objects, sweep frees the unmarked ones.

answer.text: The mark phase frees memory; the sweep phase allocates new objects

feedback.text: Mark does not free, and sweep does not allocate; it reclaims unmarked memory.
That describes reference counting, a different technique.

answer.text: The sweep phase marks reachable objects and the mark phase compacts them

feedback.text: The roles are reversed: mark marks, sweep reclaims.

generalfeedback.text: Mark-and-sweep: the mark phase marks every reachable object, then the sweep phase reclaims all objects that were not marked.

questiontext.text: Which statements about dynamic storage management and GC are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: Reference counting is an alternative to mark-and-sweep for reclaiming objects

feedback.text: Yes — both are automatic reclamation techniques.

answer.text: External fragmentation may require compaction to consolidate free space

feedback.text: Yes — compaction moves objects together to defragment the heap.

answer.text: The sweep phase marks all reachable objects

feedback.text: No — marking is the mark phase; sweep reclaims the unmarked ones.
No — best-fit reduces waste per allocation but does not eliminate fragmentation.

generalfeedback.text: Free lists and first-/best-fit drive allocation; mark-and-sweep or reference counting reclaim unreachable objects; fragmentation may need compaction.

questiontext.text: External fragmentation can leave enough total free memory yet no single block big enough, which is one reason compaction may be needed.

feedback.text: Correct — scattered free space can be consolidated by compaction.
Fragmentation really can scatter free space, motivating compaction.

questiontext.text: In mark-and-sweep, it is the sweep phase that marks all reachable objects.

feedback.text: Marking reachable objects is the mark phase; the sweep phase reclaims the rest.
Correct — the mark phase marks reachable objects; the sweep phase reclaims the unmarked ones.

questiontext.text: The garbage-collection phase that visits and flags every reachable object is called the ______ phase.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
Accepted — this is the mark-and-sweep algorithm.
Accepted — the companion phase in mark-and-sweep.
